title: The lesson opens on a baker who must total 3 boxes of 24 cookies, a problem that is too large for a known single-digit fact. It teaches the learner to split 24 into 20 and 4, multiply each part by 3, and name the two partial products 60 and 12. It then confronts the belief that 24 × 3 equals 6 × 12 by showing where that shortcut loses the tens, and it closes by checking that the learner can decompose a two-digit factor and state both partial products. (P09 edit)
